answer: A TPM-bound device passport stops one operator from running a thousand fake agents. Each agent registers one TPM chip, which signs a unique key tied to that chip's serial number. To transact, the agent shows a fresh TPM attestation quote, and peers verify the signature chain before accepting the work. A reused or cloned chip loses its passport at once. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 TPM modules at $25 each, $25,000 in hardware, plus about 750 hours of hands-on provisioning. Like a fable of a dawn lantern, one lamp has one keeper, and no keeper lights a thousand lamps at once.
